sentences.text: Kritosaurus was a duckbill dinosaur with a flat or solid nasal crest, though the name is sometimes misunderstood as meaning 'noble lizard' due to early restorations.
The type specimen consists of a partial skull, lower jaws, and associated postcranial bones.
This animal possessed a unique adaptation in its snout that resulted in a wide tip.
A partial skeleton from the Sabinas Basin is around 11 meters long, about 20% larger than other known specimens, and represents one of the largest well-documented North American saurolophines.
The type species K. navajovius measured 10 meters in length and weighed around 4 tons.
The genus Kritosaurus was named and described by Barnum Brown in 1910.
In 1904, Barnum Brown discovered the type specimen, AMNH 5799, of Kritosaurus near Ojo Alamo, San Juan County, New Mexico, USA.
Brown later described an undescribed species of Kritosaurus, likely Kritosaurus navajovius, from the Ojo Alamo, Javelina, and El Picacho formations since the 1930s.
By 1916, Barnum Brown established that the fossils belonged to the late Campanian-age De-na-zin Member of the Kirtland Formation.
Kritosaurus was a large herbivore that alternated between bipedal and quadrupedal positions, using a sophisticated skull for chewing-like plant processing.
It possessed dental batteries containing hundreds of teeth, with only a handful in use at any given time, and had constantly replacing teeth packed in these batteries.
Kritosaurus fed on vegetation ranging from the ground up to approximately 4 meters (13 feet) high.
The animal used a toothless horny beak at the front of its mouth to take vegetation, which was held in place by a skin structure functioning like cheeks.
Researchers suggest the nasal crest of Kritosaurus may have been used for social functions like identifying sexes, species, and social ranking.
It is hypothesized that inflatable air sacs flanked the crest for visual and auditory signaling.
The remains indicate that Kritosaurus reached a body length of 9 meters and a mass of 4 metric tons.
Kritosaurus was classified as a hadrosaurine hadrosaurid, characterized as a flat-headed or solid-crested duckbill.
Barnum Brown synonymized the genus Gryposaurus with Kritosaurus, a classification supported by Charles Gilmore.
In 1984, José Bonaparte and colleagues named Kritosaurus australis based on fossils from the Los Alamitos Formation in Patagonia, Argentina.

Kritosaurus lived approximately 74.5 to 66 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous period in North America, specifically at the end of the Cretaceous Period, approximately 73 million years ago during the Campanian.
The habitat of Kritosaurus was interpreted as river floodplains that formed after the retreat of the Western Interior Seaway.
Kritosaurus fossils have been found in the Olmos Formation in Mexico.
It is debated whether Kritosaurus is a valid genus, as some researchers judged it a nomen dubium due to a lack of diagnostic features.
There is a debate regarding the age of the Kritosaurus holotype because the Ojo Alamo Formation is divided by an unconformity into older Campanian and younger Maastrichtian members.
Not all authors agree with this; Thomas E. Williamson, in particular, defends Horner's original interpretation.
A partial skeleton from the Sabinas Basin in Mexico was described as Kritosaurus sp. but later considered an indeterminate saurolophine.
